tasks.short: Coordinate with developers to agree, implement and accept website designs.

steps.what: Collect current designs, requirements, open issues and delivery status.
Discuss feasibility, dependencies and trade-offs with developers.
Document agreed states, behaviours, acceptance criteria and implementation details.

loop.input: Approved design decisions, linked design states and an acceptance-criteria template.
loop.output: Draft implementation specification with source links and explicit unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate required fields and links; designer checks behaviour, accessibility and unsupported assumptions.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per specification; unresolved details return to the designer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle structure, but prose decisions require interpretation into precise interaction criteria.

steps.what: Chase dependencies and reconcile delivery updates across messages and issue records.
Review the implemented interface and agree acceptance or further changes.

tasks.design: Connect design references in {DOCS} to work items in {PROJECT}, generating a live coordination pack and dependency alerts. A bounded drafting loop prepares specifications from agreed decisions; the designer approves them and retains feasibility discussions and design acceptance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Design references, implementation decisions and delivery updates live in different places. Agreement depends on conversation, while maintaining the supporting records takes separate effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing links, templates and notification rules handle much of the coordination. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building connectors, while bounded drafting handles informal decision notes.
tasks.still_hard: Changing priorities, undocumented constraints and design intent still require discussion. Design-file access and reliable version references may be expensive to integrate.
tasks.human_edge: The designer negotiates compromises and recognises when technically correct work weakens the intended experience.

ambition.what: Resolve interaction trade-offs at each prototype checkpoint instead of waiting for final implementation.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less status chasing and more early design review with developers. The designer can gain delegated authority to accept component-level interaction changes within an agreed scope.

reach.task: Translate campaign objectives into measurable website acceptance criteria.
reach.learn: Campaign measurement, scope negotiation and the distinction between delivery and customer outcomes.

evidence.claim: Linked work records, templates and dependency notifications can replace repeated status assembly.
GitHub Copilot supports coding and review with oversight; this supports connector construction, not autonomous design acceptance.
Developer field trials report productivity gains, but do not establish a specific speedup for this coordination workflow.

assumptions: A typical team uses shared design documents, work records and chat; the shares are planning estimates.
The priors correctly suggest substantial human coordination, but record maintenance can change independently.
The solution tracks delivery items rather than individual employee productivity.
Estimates cover one team and one work-record integration; national consultation requirements may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Whether design decisions have stable links and identifiable owners.
Which interfaces and permissions are available for shared work records.
Who can approve design changes and accept implementation.
Whether national rules or existing agreements require employee consultation.
research_questions: Can source-linked specification drafts preserve interaction intent without creating extra developer clarification work?
new_work: Review generated specifications and resolve missing decisions.
Maintain document-to-work-item mappings and notification rules.
Investigate stale links and conflicting delivery updates.

tasks.short: Create visual interface concepts and revise them after stakeholder feedback.

steps.what: Review the brief, brand guidance, audience needs and existing interface patterns.
Create visual concepts using the {OTHER} interface design editor.

loop.input: Designer-selected direction, approved components, content and explicit layout constraints.
loop.output: Editable concept variants and preview pages.
loop.check: Validate component use, content completeness and responsive behaviour; designer judges hierarchy and brand fit.
loop.stop: At most three variants and one correction pass; designer continues manually if none is useful.
loop.why_not_simpler: Existing components cover routine layouts; translating a new visual direction into an editable composition needs bounded drafting.

steps.what: Present concepts and discuss stakeholder reactions and competing preferences.
Revise concepts in the {OTHER} interface design editor.
Approve the visual direction for implementation or request further revision.

tasks.design: A reference pack in {DOCS} supplies approved content, components and constraints to a bounded concept generator on {DATA_PLATFORM}. Deterministic layout controls apply repeated spacing, typography and component changes; previews and approvals stay linked in {PROJECT}. The designer shapes the direction and the marketing manager approves the concept before implementation.
tasks.previous_blocker: New concepts do not follow complete rules, and stakeholder feedback often conflicts. Even straightforward revisions require repeated layout adjustments across screen sizes.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable components and design tokens make routine variations programmable. Bounded code drafting can produce editable previews, although visual judgement remains human.
tasks.still_hard: Distinctive art direction, weak briefs and contradictory feedback remain difficult. Moving generated previews into editable design files may require custom integration.
tasks.human_edge: The designer gives a concept coherence and decides which feedback improves the experience rather than merely satisfying a preference.

ambition.what: Offer an accessibility-first concept review before campaign production begins.

tasks.altitude: The designer spends less time repeating layout edits and more time exploring and testing visual directions. They can gain authority to choose compliant component variants within approved brand guidance.

reach.task: Adapt campaign artwork into a reusable family of responsive digital assets.
reach.learn: Art direction, image rights, cropping behaviour and visual consistency across formats.

evidence.claim: Component constraints and parameterised layouts can automate repeated visual adjustments while leaving concept selection human.
GitHub Copilot can assist with preview code; its documented capabilities do not establish visual concept quality.
Playwright Test Agents can generate and repair tests; automated checks still do not establish aesthetic or usability quality.

assumptions: A usable component library exists or the pilot includes only a small component set.
Concept creation primarily happens in a design editor; the prior's meeting share is too high for this task.
Repeated revisions include programmable layout changes alongside manual creative work.
Only approved content and suitably licensed assets enter generation.
The build estimate covers one page family and does not include creating a complete brand system.
unknowns: How complete and editable the component library is.
Whether the design editor supports reliable import or programmatic updates.
Which stakeholders approve concepts and how conflicts are resolved.
Whether briefs or research contain personal data requiring GDPR controls.
Whether national consultation requirements apply to the proposed tooling.
research_questions: Do generated concepts remain editable enough to reduce total revision effort?
Which layout checks predict useful concepts, and which require direct user evaluation?
new_work: Select useful variants and remove weak or misleading concepts.
Maintain component constraints, asset permissions and preview templates.
Check accessibility and responsive behaviour beyond automated findings.

tasks.short: Keep web technology and design practice current through reading, learning and professional exchange.

steps.what: Find updates through subscriptions and the {OTHER} research reader.
Select learning topics relevant to current projects and skill gaps.

loop.input: Allowlisted technical updates, declared learning goals and non-confidential project topics.
loop.output: A ranked shortlist with relevance reasons, dates and source links.
loop.check: Check source availability and duplicates; designer checks relevance against original material.
loop.stop: One weekly batch with at most ten shortlisted items; inaccessible sources remain unsummarised.
loop.why_not_simpler: Subscription filters handle known topics, but relevance across changing technical prose needs semantic classification.

steps.what: Study technical material and practise unfamiliar techniques.
Attend workshops or professional groups and discuss practical experience.
Record useful findings and choose a small application to current work.

tasks.design: Configure subscriptions into a personal reading queue and use a bounded relevance loop on {DATA_PLATFORM} to prepare a source-linked shortlist. A small learning register in {DOCS} connects practice examples to experiments in {PROJECT}. Reading, practice and professional exchange remain the designer's work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Information is abundant, but relevance changes with projects and existing knowledge. Collecting more material does not create understanding.
tasks.enabler_now: Feed filters and duplicate removal are straightforward configuration. A bounded classifier can explain why an unfamiliar update may matter without replacing the source material.
tasks.still_hard: Assessing source quality, gaining deep skills and judging when to change practice still take time. Restricted publications and changing terminology limit automatic collection.
tasks.human_edge: The designer connects new knowledge to lived project experience and learns through practice and discussion.

ambition.what: Provide a monthly evidence-backed web-practice clinic for the marketing team.

tasks.altitude: The week includes less searching and a more deliberate practice session. No implementation decision rights change; recommendations still follow the team's technical review process.

reach.task: Assess how new browser and rendering practices affect discoverability.
reach.learn: Crawlability, performance measurement and evidence-based search experiments.

evidence.claim: Subscriptions, duplicate removal and a learning register can reduce information gathering without automating learning.
Source-linked relevance ranking is a plausible bounded model use; the digest supplies no measured case for designer learning outcomes.

assumptions: Shares describe an average learning cycle, including occasional workshops, rather than every learning session.
The shortlist uses declared interests rather than inferred employee performance.
Most learning sources are public or already licensed.
There is no mandatory certification process in this task.
unknowns: Which subscriptions and learning resources are available.
Whether employees have protected time and budget for practice.
Whether learning records are private or visible to managers.
Whether national rules require consultation over learning analytics or employee records.
research_questions: Does the shortlist increase useful practice and retention rather than merely increasing reading volume?
new_work: Maintain source subscriptions and learning goals.
Check original sources when recommendations are surprising.
Remove stale topics and record whether practice recommendations helped.

tasks.short: Answer website user inquiries and configure reliable routine responses.

steps.what: Read incoming inquiries and identify their topic, urgency and responsible team.

loop.input: Inquiry text with unnecessary personal data removed, plus approved routing categories.
loop.output: Suggested category, urgency and responsible queue.
loop.check: Validate category and queue; route uncertain, sensitive or complaint-related cases for human triage.
loop.stop: One classification attempt per inquiry; ambiguity goes to the shared review queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Forms and address rules handle explicit categories; free-text descriptions need semantic classification.

steps.what: Find relevant guidance, known issues and current website information.
Compose an answer or adapt an existing response template.

loop.input: Inquiry, approved answer evidence and response policy; exact routine matches use templates.
loop.output: Draft answer with internal evidence links or an explicit escalation reason.
loop.check: Require evidence for instructions and claims; prohibit unsupported account details, promises and policy exceptions.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; missing evidence or unresolved checks trigger human handling.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover routine cases; varied descriptions sometimes require a source-grounded explanation.

steps.what: Check the answer and send it to the user.
Resolve ambiguous cases or arrange specialist follow-up.
Record the outcome and label recurring website problems.

tasks.design: Connect {EMAIL} to {HELPDESK}, configure routing, approved response templates and outcome logging, and retrieve guidance from {DOCS} and {CMS}. Bounded loops classify free text and draft evidence-backed answers; novel drafts require approval before sending, while explicitly approved routine templates can send automatically. Recurring topics create website friction records in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Shared mailboxes mix repeat questions with ambiguous problems. Guidance becomes stale, and the designer often reconstructs both the answer and its history.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured intake, templates and case records already handle much of the workflow. Small classification and drafting loops can handle wording variation without unrestricted access or autonomous problem solving.
tasks.still_hard: Account-specific problems, accessibility barriers and dissatisfied users need careful handling. Incorrect or outdated guidance can make a fluent answer harmful.
tasks.human_edge: The designer recognises frustration and underlying interface failures, and takes responsibility for exceptions that standard guidance cannot resolve.

ambition.what: Deliver a weekly website-friction brief that turns recurring inquiries into prioritised interface fixes.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from repeated explanations toward difficult cases and prevention. The designer can gain delegated authority to prioritise small usability fixes within an agreed maintenance budget.

reach.task: Turn recurring website questions into tested help articles.
reach.learn: Task-based instructions, plain language, content ownership and review schedules.

evidence.claim: TOPdesk suggests ticket categories and priorities and drafts knowledge items for review; this supports bounded assistance.
Configured response templates, queue routing and case logging can automate routine inquiry administration.
GDPR applies to personal data in inquiries; collection, access, model processing and retention need appropriate controls.
AI Act Article 50 includes transparency obligations for direct interaction with AI; a user-facing conversational assistant needs assessment.

assumptions: This task covers website inquiries reaching the designer, not the entire customer service operation.
Email and case screens dominate actual handling; the prior's document share overstates document use.
The sending gate applies to generated and exceptional answers; preapproved routine templates use explicit automatic-send rules.
The send-step remaining time is a blended planning estimate across routine and reviewed cases.
Steps describe average case effort; only some inquiries require specialist follow-up.
Employee productivity scoring is outside scope; national consultation requirements still need checking.
unknowns: Inquiry volume, repeat-topic share and the proportion needing account-specific information.
Which guidance is approved, current and owned.
Whether a shared case system already captures the mailbox.
Which responses can be preapproved for automatic sending.
Permitted processing locations, retention periods and model access to personal data.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for the proposed records and reporting.
research_questions: What proportion of inquiries can use exact approved templates without clarification?
Does source-grounded drafting reduce handling time without increasing incorrect advice or repeat contacts?
new_work: Review generated answers and handle uncertain routing.
Refresh templates, evidence links and escalation rules.
Sample automatically sent routine responses for errors.
Maintain access controls, retention settings and the website-friction backlog.

role.altitude: The designer spends more time shaping experiences, testing decisions and resolving difficult user problems. With explicit delegation, they can accept component-level changes and prioritise small usability fixes; broader brand, budget and release authority still requires assignment.
reach: Marketing manager: connect campaign objectives to website acceptance criteria.
Graphic designer: extend visual directions into reusable responsive assets.
Search marketing strategist: evaluate technical changes through discoverability experiments.
Technical writer: turn inquiry patterns into maintained user guidance.
skills_to_grow: Structured interaction specifications and component systems.
Accessibility evaluation with direct user testing.
Source-grounded model review and bounded automation design.
Workflow configuration, integration scoping and exception handling.
Experiment design and interpretation of user outcomes.
GDPR-aware handling of inquiries and research material.
role.ambitious_version: Run a continuous website improvement service that connects campaign goals, design concepts, developer delivery and recurring user problems. Use the saved coordination and response effort to test accessibility and usability earlier, with clear authority over a limited improvement budget.
